title: Preconditions and Postconditions
definition: Preconditions define what must hold before an operation, and postconditions define the guarantees expected after successful completion.
purpose: Separate valid-input obligations from the result an algorithm promises to establish.
history: Contract-based correctness reasoning formalizes the relationship between initial conditions, execution, and guaranteed results.
mental_model: The precondition is the entry gate; the postcondition is the observable exit promise.
analogy: A service agreement states what the requester must provide and what the provider returns; the analogy stops where software state and failure paths require greater precision.
industry_notes: Explicit contracts improve review, testing, integration, and change impact analysis even when no formal contract language is used.
ai_notes: AI suggestions must not silently widen preconditions or weaken postconditions.
interview_notes: Ask which obligations belong to the caller and which guarantees belong to the algorithm.
exercise_candidates: Classify statements as preconditions, postconditions, or implementation details
project_candidates: Specify instruction input and final state contracts
